title: Insecure Deserialization in Java
description: A Java service deserializes untrusted bytes from the request body, allowing gadget-chain attacks.
owasp: A08:2021 - Software and Data Integrity Failures

finding.title: Insecure Deserialization
finding.description: The app calls readObject() on bytes sent by the client, giving the attacker control over which classes are instantiated.
finding.why_dangerous: Java deserialization can trigger gadget chains that execute arbitrary code.
finding.impact: Remote code execution, denial of service, application compromise.
finding.fix: Never deserialize untrusted data; parse JSON/XML with explicit schemas and allowlists.
learning_example: A crafted serialized stream can run code without any application logic
Replacing ObjectInputStream with a validated JSON mapper removes the class-instantiation surface

checklist: Use explicit, validated data formats (JSON/XML) with strict schemas
Apply allowlists for any object types you do accept
Restrict the JVM classpath reachable by deserialization
